terms.comment: In particular a foot soldier, as against eques (Lewis & Short); a private, mīles gregārius; to serve as a soldier, mīlitāre (Traupman 187).

phrases.latin: malus mīles est quī imperātōrem gemēns sequitur
phrases.english: he is a poor soldier who follows his general grumbling

sources: Lewis & Short: miles
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 187–188, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
